title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Standards, templates, operating procedures and canonical fixes for Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site publishing, and top support issues.
body:
Overview

Purpose
This page defines standards and reusable templates for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues with fixes. The goals are consistent reader experience, faster onboarding of new SDKs and integrations, and reduced support-to-engineering churn.

Scope
- All public-facing SDK guides (JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, and community SDKs)
- Quickstarts and sample apps hosted in the docs repo and templates catalog
- Canonical API examples used in the docs site and README snippets
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, versioning, rollouts)
- Top support issues + canonical fixes for common developer workflows

Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience)
- Documentation author: SDK owner or feature PM (see template below)
- Reviewers: DevEx tech writer + SDK engineering lead
- Publishing SLA: changes to SDK guides or quickstarts must be staged and reviewed within 3 business days for urgent fixes, and within 10 business days for routine updates.

Doc Types and When to Use Them
- SDK Guide: detailed reference for an SDK (installation, auth, models, examples, edge cases, troubleshooting). Use for maintained SDKs.
- Quickstart: "Hello world" flows (5–10 minute), minimal copy/paste to make first API call. Use for onboarding and product pages.
- Template App: 1–3 small apps showing real use cases (chat widget, summarizer pipeline). Use for deeper learning and reference projects.
- API Example Snippet: short code or curl snippets used inline across docs. Keep < 20 lines.

Content Standards (applies to all doc types)
- Tone: engineering-friendly, direct, and actionable. Use first-level audience: software engineers and ML engineers.
- Structure: short intro; prerequisites; step-by-step examples; troubleshooting; next steps.
- Code style: provide both JavaScript and Python SDK examples when applicable. Use the newest stable SDK version.
- Security: do not include real API keys. Show usage with environment variables.
- Tests: all quickstarts and template apps must include a lightweight smoke test (CI job) that runs at least once per week.

Templates
1) SDK Guide Template (use for each SDK)- Title and short description- Supported platforms and compatibility matrix (versions)- Installation (package manager commands)- Authentication (env vars, KMS notes)- Core API overview (key classes/functions)- Common patterns (chat, streaming, embeddings)- Edge cases and performance tips- Troubleshooting table- Changelog and migration notes

2) Quickstart Template- Prerequisites (account, API key, node/python version)- Install- Minimal call (30–50 lines)- Expected output- Troubleshooting/FAQ- Cleanup

Minimal Quickstart examples (copy/paste)
JavaScript (Node 18+)
# install
npm install @redwood/inference-sdk
# set env
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REPLACE_ME

import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
async function main() {
  const res = await client.chat.create({
    model: 'redwood-1.0-chat',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a one-paragraph summary of Redwood Inference.' }],
  });
  console.log(res.choices[0].message.content);
}
main();

Python (3.10+)
# install
pip install redwood-inference
# set env
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REPLACE_ME

from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-1.0-chat', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Write a one-paragraph summary of Redwood Inference.'}])
print(resp.choices[0].message['content'])

API Examples and Patterns
- Auth patterns: prefer environment variables or secret-backed config. In docs show both: env var + CLI to set config.
- Streaming responses: show example with backpressure handling in JS and Python.
- Function/tool calls: provide a JSON schema example and a safe execution pattern with timeouts and validation.
- Embeddings + similarity: demonstrate batching and minimal latency guidelines (batch size recommendations are in the performance section).

Docs Site Operating Procedures
1) Branching and Drafting
- Use feature branches under docs/* or sdk/* in the docs repo.
- Put all images under /assets/<feature> and reference with relative paths.

2) Review Process
- Create a PR with the doc changes and tag @devex, @sdk-owner, and one technical reviewer.
- DevEx writer runs editorial pass for clarity and tone.
- SDK owner runs code example smoke tests and signs off.
- Review checklist: accuracy, tested examples, security (no keys), accessibility alt text for images.

3) Release and Rollout
- Merge to main triggers staging build. Staging must pass smoke tests (example scripts + lint).
- Canary publish: docs changes are staged to a 5% bucket for 24 hours for high-impact changes (API surface or authentication).
- Full publish: after 24 hours and no regressions, promote to 100%.

4) Rollback
- If regressions detected, revert PR and re-run staging smoke tests. The rollback owner is the DevEx lead on call.

5) Versioning
- All SDK guides must indicate the SDK version. For breaking changes, include migration steps and a migration badge at the top of the doc.

Canonical Troubleshooting and Top Support Issues (current top 12)
Format: ISSUE | SYMPTOMS | LIKELY CAUSE | CANONICAL FIX | OWNER | ROLLBACK NOTES

1) Auth errors: 401/403 when calling API | API returns 401 or 403 | Missing/expired API key, wrong env var name, or org-level access restriction | Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, check org key scope in Console, rotate key, update env var in deployment | DevEx + Platform API | Rollback: restore previous key and re-deploy config

2) SDK mismatch: examples break with TypeError | Example API shapes changed in a new SDK release | Docs snippet using old SDK patterns | Update examples to latest SDK pattern, run smoke tests, add migration note | SDK owner | Rollback: pin docs to previous SDK version and publish

3) Streaming hang / partial output | stream stalls or hangs indefinitely | Missing read loop or backpressure handling; server-side transient issue | Add recommended client loop with timeout/reconnect; check runtime incident dashboard | Eng-serving-runtime + DevEx | Rollback: revert streaming example changes and re-add known-good snippet

4) Rate limit (429) in quickstarts | Calls intermittently fail with 429 | Quickstart calls are too aggressive for new accounts or CI | Add exponential backoff and advise sample token limits in quickstart prerequisites | DevEx | Rollback: reduce sample concurrency in example code

5) Large response truncation | content cut off mid-sentence | Client-side read buffer or server token limit mismatch | Document response streaming and set stream=true; show chunked handling | SDK owner + Eng-runtime | Rollback: provide earlier non-streaming example if needed

6) Embeddings poor recall | Similarity search returns low-quality results | Missing normalization, wrong model, or no preprocessing | Recommend model selection table, preprocessing steps, and example batching code | Applied ML | Rollback: point docs to previous recommendation and include note

7) Local dev CORS errors on example apps | Browser blocks requests | Quickstart uses direct browser calls instead of proxying via server | Update quickstart to use a server-side proxy example and mention CORS policy | DevEx | Rollback: re-add a server-side proxy snippet and warning

8) Test flakiness in CI for quickstarts | CI smoke test intermittently fails | Tests rely on live API without retries or deterministic inputs | Add deterministic inputs, mock option, or test API keys with predictable quotas | DevEx + Infra | Rollback: revert CI changes and re-run with mock tests

9) Misleading error messages | Users see vague 500/502 messages | Server returns generic errors or SDK surface hides inner exception | Update SDK to surface structured error object and update docs with example diagnostics | SDK owner + Eng-runtime | Rollback: revert SDK surface change if it breaks integrations

10) Outdated screenshots | Console UI screenshots no longer match | Console changed layout | Flag and replace screenshots during release; add screenshot review step to checklist | DevEx + Product | Rollback: revert image change and add note about UI version

11) Missing accessibility attributes | Images or code blocks missing alt/text | Author oversight | Add accessibility checks to PR checklist; templated alt text fields in quickstart template | DevEx | Rollback: fix images and re-publish

12) Function/tool calling misuse | Unsafe execution of returned tool commands | Example executes unvalidated tool output | Add validation step, timeouts, and safe execution examples (sandboxed) | Applied ML + DevEx | Rollback: mark examples as deprecated and replace with safe pattern

Canonical Fix Templates
- For each issue above, a one-paragraph remediation template is stored under /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/remediation-templates. Use these templates when responding to support tickets and PRs.

Troubleshooting Table (example)
| Symptom | Quick check | Fix | Time to resolution |
| ------- | ----------- | ---- | ------------------ |
| 401 on startup | env REDWOOD_API_KEY set? | Export correct key, ensure key scope | 10–30 min |
| Streaming stalls | run sample stream tool | add timeout and reconnect logic | 30–90 min |

CI and Test Requirements for Docs PRs
- Every quickstart or template app that includes network calls must provide either a recorded mock response or a test API key with limited quota in CI.
- Smoke tests must run in staging on PR and in weekly cadence on main.

Monitoring and Alerting
- Key doc metrics: broken examples (PR test failure), example-coverage %, docs build failures.
- Alerts: build failure alert to #devex on Slack; example test flakiness alerts to #devex-ci.

On-call and Escalation
- DevEx on-call rotates weekly. For doc regressions that cause production impact (e.g., auth guidance causing mass customer lockouts), escalate to Eng SRE and Product via the incident channel and follow the incident runbook.

Appendix: Example PR checklist (copy into PR template)
1) Code examples run locally and in CI
2) No secrets in PR
3) Images under assets and alt text added
4) Reviewer(s) assigned: DevEx + SDK owner
5) Smoke tests included or mocked
6) Docs site lint pass

Change Log
- 2026-02-10: Published initial version with templates and top-12 support issues.
- 2026-03-01: Added canary rollout step and updated JS quickstart to new SDK naming conventions.

If you have questions or want a new quickstart template (e.g., React widget or serverless example), open a PR and tag @Aisha Patel and @DevEx.
